findings.claim: The code docstring asserts (lines 116-117): 'Anything else stays ``not-ok`` - a real failure must never be laundered into "the environment did it"', and the commit says 'A real defect cannot be laundered into "the environment did it"'. findings.md line 37 repeats it ('真失败绝不会被洗成"环境问题"').
findings.counter_evidence: A REAL product defect whose collection error text contains a listed marker is recorded as blocked. `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_real_pytest.py` builds a one-line suite that reproduces a product-side path bug (`Path('config/filing_fetch.toml').read_text()` looked up against the wrong root) and feeds the genuine `pytest -q --tb=short` output to `_suite_outcome`: observed 't_product_path_bug.py :: real pytest rc=2 -> ok=False status=blocked', detail 'T3 suite could not run here (exit 2; environment: no such file) - no test reached a verdict', with the real output line 'E   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: \'config\\filing_fetch.toml\''. The same probe shows a fixture/setup error from the code under test ('ERROR at setup of test_download - ConnectionResetError') -> blocked. Any no-verdict error containing 'not found', 'no such file', 'connection', 'network', 'permission denied', 'credentials', 'timed out', 'unauthorized' or 'not installed' is attributed to the machine, including errors raised BY the product under test.
findings.required_fix: Make the blocked branch evidence-based instead of text-based. Cheapest options: (a) require the marker to appear in a frame outside the code under test (pytest's traceback names the failing file, so 'tests/...' vs product path is decidable); (b) let the suite emit an explicit machine-readable 'environment unavailable' banner (e.g. a sentinel line the harness requires) and drop the free-text markers; (c) if the heuristic is kept, record WHICH word matched in the alert/ledger (it is currently only in `detail`, and only the alert journal keeps it) and add a third state for 'no verdict, cause unattributed'. Until then, do not state the absolute guarantee in the docstring or the commit message.
findings.residual: Both statuses write ok=False, so no green gate results from this; the harm is attribution inside the assurance record - an operator is directed to fix the environment while the product is broken, which is precisely the failure mode F-B01-10-classify set out to remove. I could not construct a case where this produces ok=True.

findings.claim: blocked 'says the suite could not be evaluated here (no credentials, no tool, nothing collected)' (docstring lines 111-112) and the commit's rule is 'non-zero with NO test reaching a verdict -> blocked when ... the output carries an environment marker'.
findings.counter_evidence: Real, local, non-network failures whose text matches NO marker, each observed as ok=False status=not-ok (a statement about the product): (1) the production download tool is missing and launched the way the suite launches it - `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_winerror.py` -> 'rc=2 -> ok=False status=not-ok', real output 'E   FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] <localized Chinese message>' (on this machine the Windows API message is LOCALIZED, so even 'cannot find the file' would not match); (2) pytest itself missing - same probe, `python -B -m not_a_module_at_all` -> 'rc=1 -> not-ok', stderr 'C:\\Miniconda\\python.exe: No module named not_a_module_at_all'; (3) a required env var absent - real pytest run t_envvar.py -> 'rc=2 -> not-ok', 'E   RuntimeError: FILING_FETCH_WIKI is not set'. Also demonstrated: an environment error that DOES match ('RuntimeError: production download tool not found') is flipped to not-ok when any captured-stdout line reads like a verdict count - t_flip.py printed 'adapter: 3 passed validation checks, 0 failed', pytest shows it under 'Captured stdout' in the error report, and the observed status became 'not-ok' instead of 'blocked' (constructed text, but real pytest output and a realistic product log line).
findings.required_fix: Either widen the evidence base or stop substring-matching free text: prefer structured signals (pytest exit codes 3/4/5, the final summary line, a suite-emitted environment banner). If markers stay, cover the observed wordings ('is not set', 'No module named', 'Access is denied', 'No space left', 'WinError 2', localized variants) and require the verdict count to come from the summary line rather than anywhere in the log.
findings.residual: The narrow list is documented as a deliberate choice ('Deliberately narrow ... the conservative direction for a release gate'), which is why this is P2 rather than P1 - but the docstring's own parenthetical claims missing-tool coverage that the most realistic missing-tool output does not get. Both directions of error coexist: the same heuristic launders product defects (B-VR903-01) and mislabels environment failures.

findings.counter_evidence: File timestamps: report weekly-run-20260913T194234Z.log created/last written 2026-09-13 20:43:32.422450 (+0100), weekly_manifest.json last written 20:43:54.790632 - a 22.37 s gap - although run_weekly writes the ledger on the line immediately after the report (lines 187-188) with nothing between them except three `_head()` git calls, which I measured at 0.064 + 0.132 + 0.151 = 0.35 s total (`python %TEMP%\zr903_review\head_timing.py`). abdd168 was committed at 20:43:53 (+0100), i.e. 1.8 s BEFORE the ledger's final write, and the two logs were committed 7 s later in 9f849f9 (20:44:01). findings.area: machine-scoped constant leaked by the new persisted report (tools/weekly_t3_schedule.py:167 writes argv; 205-217 registers an ABSOLUTE script path)
findings.claim: _write_suite_report's docstring (lines 154-159, and abdd168's message) justifies the bare file name because 'the ledger is a TRACKED artifact, so an absolute path would bake this machine's user profile into the repository' (the F-B01-9 class).
findings.counter_evidence: The report BODY records `argv=sys.argv`, the report sits next to the ledger and is tracked (both weekly-run-*.log are in `git ls-files`, and `git check-ignore` reports them as not ignored), and the registered scheduled task invokes the script by its resolved absolute path (`New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute <python> -Argument '"<Path(__file__).resolve()>" run-weekly'`, lines 206-207). Simulating exactly that argv (`python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_argv_leak.py`) produced a persisted report whose first lines are 'run_id=... status=ok ok=True exit_code=0' / 'argv=[\'C:\\\\Users\\\\<profile>\\\\Projects\\\\revenue-forecast\\\\tools\\\\weekly_t3_schedule.py\', \'run-weekly\']' -> 'contains the absolute profile path: True', while the same run's ledger field stayed relative ('report_path': 'weekly-run-20260913T212729Z.log'). The two committed logs escape this only because they were manual runs from the repo root (`argv=['tools/weekly_t3_schedule.py', 'run-weekly']`).
findings.required_fix: Do not persist argv verbatim into a tracked file: record the subcommand only (argv[1:]) or a redacted/relative form, or write the report outside the tracked tree (e.g. a gitignored per-run directory like the daily runner's `assurance/runs/<run_id>/`), or add a report-path redaction step before the file is committed.
findings.residual: The ledger's own report_path field is clean, so abdd168's stated protection for the ledger holds; the leak is in the sibling tracked artifact introduced by e45bace and only materialises when a scheduled/absolute-path run's report is committed (the operator does commit these logs - 9f849f9).

findings.area: harness failure modes leave no record (run_weekly / _run_t3_suite timeout, lines 96-100, 179-195)
findings.claim: The module docstring enumerates what run-weekly records (ledger, alert, report) and implies a blocked/failed run is always recorded; nothing documents a run that never reaches write_ledger.
findings.counter_evidence: `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_order.py` case 1 stubs `_run_t3_suite` to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired (the real 3600 s timeout in `_run_t3_suite` is exactly this path) and the observed result is 'raised TimeoutExpired out of run_weekly' with files: [] -> no ledger, no alert, no report. The same is true of any unhandled exception before write_ledger (probe case 2: crash between report and ledger -> one orphan report file, ledger absent, alerts absent). Because freshness_status reads the PREVIOUS ledger, `verify` can keep reporting fresh + release_gate=True (up to the 7-day MAX_AGE_DAYS window) while this week's run died, and the JSON record contains no trace of the crash.
findings.required_fix: Wrap the run in try/except: on TimeoutExpired/OSError/subprocess failure record a blocked entry (ok=False, report_path with the exception text, alert status=blocked) so a hang or a git failure is a recorded state rather than silence; and make the report/ledger write failure paths leave a marker instead of only stderr (see B-VR903-07).
findings.residual: Pre-existing (not introduced by tonight's three commits), and the Task Scheduler's own last-run result would show the non-zero exit - but that signal lives outside the assurance record this work is about, and the docstring's blocked definition ('fully skipped, nothing collected, or a collection error carrying an environment marker') does not cover it. Not verified: whether a SYSTEM-context git failure (the GP-009 class) can also abort between report and ledger.

findings.area: best-effort report write leaves a dangling pointer (lines 171-176)

findings.counter_evidence: `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_order.py` case 4 makes Path.write_text raise OSError for .log only: observed ledger report_path 'weekly-run-20260913T212415Z.log' with file exists=False, run_weekly rc=3, alert {status: not-ok, exit_code: 3}, and the only notice is the harness's own stderr ('warning: could not persist the suite report: disk full') which the scheduled task discards. findings.area: run_id collision / report overwrite (run_id from start time, line 180; target name line 161)
findings.claim: The report 'always sits next to the ledger, so the name resolves unambiguously' (docstring lines 156-158).
findings.counter_evidence: `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_order.py` case 3 freezes the clock to one second and runs run_weekly twice: both runs get run_id 20260913T120000Z, produce ONE report file, and the second run's output overwrites the first - observed 'report files after run A: 1 after run B: 1' and 'run A's evidence still on disk: False'. The journal keeps A's not-ok entry while the ledger (B, ok=true) carries the SAME run_id, so the two tracked artifacts contradict each other for one identity, and the alert's report pointer resolves to the other run's report.
findings.required_fix: Make the id unique (append a short random/PID suffix or a counter) or refuse to overwrite an existing `weekly-run-<run_id>.log`; a collision is cheap to detect (target.exists()) and should at least be recorded.
findings.residual: Needs two overlapping starts inside the same wall-clock second (the suite itself runs ~1 min), so it is a manual/overlap scenario rather than a scheduled one; the file-name ambiguity is limited to that second.

suspicions.evidence: `python %TEMP%\zr903_review\probe_classifier.py` (11 hand-built environment outputs) plus REAL local process output in `probe_winerror.py` and `probe_real_pytest.py`: missing download tool launched via subprocess -> real 'E FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] <localized>' -> rc=2 not-ok; pytest itself missing -> 'No module named not_a_module_at_all' -> rc=1 not-ok; 'RuntimeError: FILING_FETCH_WIKI is not set' -> rc=2 not-ok; 'PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied' -> not-ok; 'OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device' -> not-ok; pytest INTERNALERROR (rc=3) and KeyboardInterrupt (rc=2) -> not-ok. Match-directed: 'timed out', 'connection', 'not found', 'no such file' and 'no tests ran' do produce blocked.
suspicions.why: The marker list is a free-text heuristic over a localized, tool-dependent message space, so several canonical 'could not run here' failures are recorded as statements about the product - the opposite of the change's documented intent. Note the localization: on this non-English Windows the WinError-2 message carries no English marker at all, so the gap is wider here than on an English host. Recorded as B-VR903-02.

suspicions.evidence: Real pytest runs (`probe_real_pytest.py`): a product-side path bug at collection ('FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: config\\filing_fetch.toml', rc=2) -> blocked 'environment: no such file'; a fixture error raised by the code under test ('ERROR at setup of test_download - ConnectionResetError', rc=1) -> blocked 'environment: connection'; the hand-built analogue 'RuntimeError: adapter config not found' -> blocked 'environment: not found'. Both files are in the real pytest error report, i.e. no contrived packaging was needed.
suspicions.why: A genuine product defect that breaks collection/setup with a marker-flavoured message is attributed to the machine, and the harness's own detail line then asserts 'no test reached a verdict' (false for setup errors - see the claims_verified entry). Impact is bounded because blocked still blocks the ZR-902 gate (ok=False in both branches), so this is misattribution, not a green gate; the record nevertheless sends the reader to the environment instead of the code. Recorded as B-VR903-01 (P1) for the false stated guarantee.

suspicions.evidence: VERDICT_COUNTS is matched against the whole stdout+stderr. Real pytest output proves the flip is reachable in the blocked->not-ok direction: t_flip.py raises 'RuntimeError: production download tool not found' at collection (which alone matches 'not found' -> blocked) while printing 'adapter: 3 passed validation checks, 0 failed'; pytest shows that line under '------------------------------- Captured stdout -------------------------------' inside the error report, and the observed classification became 'not-ok' (detail 'T3 suite exit 2'). The reverse (false PASS) is constructible - rc=0, '4 skipped in 0.10s' plus a stray '1 passed ...' line yields ok=True via the verdict branch - but I could NOT reach it with a real pytest run: in the skip-only experiment pytest discarded the module-level print entirely (observed output was only 'ss [100%] / 2 skipped in 0.02s'), and filing-fetch's pyproject.toml sets no addopts and no conftest/plugin prints counts. Also noted: the verdict regex is case-SENSITIVE while markers are matched case-insensitively, so '4 PASSED' would not count as a verdict.
suspicions.why: Confirmed for the direction that matters here: a product log line hidden in a captured-stdout block silently converts an environment failure into a product failure. The dangerous direction (a suite that never ran recorded as ok) requires an uncaptured writer (plugin/terminal-summary hook) that I could not demonstrate, so I did not raise it as a finding; the docstring's absolute 'never a pass' would need re-wording if such a writer is ever added.

notes: For the author, in rough priority order. (1) The classifier's two failure directions are the same defect: a free-text marker list over a localized, tool-dependent message space. If you keep the heuristic, require an explicit environment signal (a sentinel the suite prints, or 'no test collected/ran' plus a pytest exit code) instead of free text, and put the matched word into the alert entry rather than only into `detail`. (2) Never hand-adjust a tracked ledger: B-VR903-04 shows a 22 s gap that no code path in run_weekly can account for (measured 0.35 s of intervening git work), and the findings table and abdd168's message state opposite causal orders; whichever is right, the record should say how the field was produced. (3) B-VR903-05 is the F-B01-9 class re-entering through the door e45bace opened: the tracked report body carries argv, and the scheduled task passes an absolute path; redact it or move the report to a gitignored directory. (4) Two gaps already flagged OUTSIDE this repo and still open, so I did not raise them as findings: company-wiki docs/plans/painpoint-outcome-audit-2026-09-05/assurance-audit.md:46 and findings.md:57 note (a) that `_suite_outcome` records '1 passed, 2 skipped' as ok even though the acceptance wants no skipped required market, and (b) that run_weekly returns proc.returncode, which is 0 for the all-skipped/blocked branch, so Task Scheduler reports success while the gate is blocked - tonight's change kept both behaviours (the return value path at lines 189-195 is `return proc.returncode`; I confirmed it empirically by running a blocked case, `probe_blocked_rc.py`: 'blocked run: run_weekly returned 0' with ledger ok=False and alert status=blocked, so the Task Scheduler result is now the only remaining 'silent success' signal for a blocked run). (5) The weekly ledger still has no status field: the blocked/not-ok distinction lives only in weekly_alert.jsonl and the report body, so a reader of the tracked ledger alone (or of its history) cannot tell the two apart - defensible because write_ledger's schema is shared with daily/monthly and both statuses are ok=False, but worth a sentence in the docstring. (6) My own two mistakes are recorded in independence_statement: an English-only WinError-2 probe string (corrected to a real subprocess run, which showed the message is localized) and a UTF-16 PowerShell redirect that produced a bogus blob-hash mismatch (corrected with git hash-object). Both corrections changed the review: the localization widened S1, and the hash check confirmed the working tree is byte-identical to HEAD.
